items.title: Stephen Thomas, Inspector OPP and Board Chair Campbell re: 2023
notes: report

Stephen Thomas, Inspector OPP noted reporting will look differently next year in accordance with the provisions of the New Community Safety Act. He provided highlights and statistics regarding the activities of the various units, including the Street Crime Unit, the Community Response Unit, and the Marine Patrol Unit.

S. Thomas noted the continuation of the Ride and Impact programs and the opening of Collision Reporting Centres. He noted the work of the Auxiliary unit and provided notable statistics and trends regarding property crime, fraud, theft, mischief, shoplifting, drug crime and motor vehicle collisions.
He responded to questions regarding the success of the Impact Unit and the value they bring to the community and the officers, and monitoring of dangerous and repeat accident locations.
County Councillor and Board Chair Earl Campbell provided a brief overview of the launch of the new automated speed enforcement cameras coming to each municipality within the County.

items.title: Cemetery Product, Services and Fees Review report -
notes: LEES+Associates
Report from L. Rogerson, Manager of Parks
Presentation from Kelsey Walker and Jennifer Thibert, LEES + Associates
Lucas Rogerson, Manager of Parks introduced consultants Kelsey Walker and Jennifer Thibert, LEES + Associates.

Kelsey Walker and Jennifer Thibert, LEES + Associates provided an overview of the report, indicating the primary objectives in developing this Cemetery Product, Services and Fees Review are a) ensure there are relevant and appropriate products and services to serve Centre Wellington families and b) ensure cemetery fees are in line with the local market.

The consultants outlined the current offerings and key findings, including a) the Township’s cemeteries currently offer a similar range of interment services, inventory and memorialization options, b) Belsyde Cemetery’s burial lots are nearly depleted and c) consider new offerings to attract the interest of community members.

The consultants outlined their recommendations in the short term and long term and responded to questions regarding various green burial options, impact of prepaid funerals on the report recommendations, revenue neutral approach vs alignment with other cemeteries, and provided details on a non-resident premium.

items.title: 2024 Urban Forestry Update Report
notes: Report L. Rogerson, Manager of Parks
Lucas Rogerson, Manager of Parks provided an overview of the report, outlining the division compliment, the objectives of the public forest policy and the details regarding the public tree by-law.

Todd Fritzley, Urban Forestry Coordinator provided an overview of the activities in 2024, including an educational workshop on pruning and chainsaw use, the pruning and removal programs, the yearly plantings and stump removals, and tree maintenance in parks and along roadways.
Staff highlighted the tracking of service requests, the development of a digital tree inventory, including the health of the tree, and outlined the goals and objectives for 2025.

Staff responded to questions regarding the replacement of trees removed and the planting policy, adequate budget, inclusion of new tree species, and the replacement of trees in the rural area and roadways.
Mayor Watters called for a recess at 5:25 pm, the meeting resumed at 5:32pm.
